title: A question regarding Isabel Reyes and her father / Sicario: Day of the Soldado (2018)

commenti.body:
Del Toro’s character is motivated by his daughter’s horrific and obtuse murder by members of a drug cartel at some point before the first film. Everything he does in the first film, including using/“rescuing” Emily Blunt’s character, is connected to that lost relationship.

In the second film, Brolin’s character leverages that trauma to get Del Toro’s character to help him kidnap the daughter of a cartel member to foment a cartel war. Del Toro’s character knows she will be killed in the violence their actions inspire. He doesn’t want to return her to Mexico because she, like Blunt’s character, causes him to remember those paternal feelings.

Thank you for your reply.

That I do understand, but what I do not is, what danger would be there for Isabel, if she were to reunite with his father again? I mean, she was fine before, living her every day life.

> she was fine before

Del Toro and Brolin's characters started a war between multiple cartels, the Mexican government, and the US government. Moner's character wasn't fine before but if she goes back to Mexico she's the daughter of someone fighting a war living in a warzone.

Del Toro doesn't want her to die, so he works to keep her where she's safe.

Thank you kindly for your reply.

I think you are right!
